question: Does the exact frozen official Example_Rotary sensor produce legal GenericModelOutput Writer callbacks when only the execution lifecycle is changed from synchronous standalone updates to NVIDIA's tested async Kit lifecycle?
why: The v2 local-official control created the sensor, attached the Writer and completed 300 synchronous standalone updates, but received zero callbacks and logged Writer-drain timeouts. A read-only audit of NVIDIA's bundled test_lidar_sensor.py shows that the actual Writer unit test is an omni.kit.test.AsyncTestCase that waits for viewport readiness and advances with next_update_async. This one-factor A/B is required before concluding that the whole host/headless Replicator runtime is broken.

frozen_control.scene: The same official four-cube layout used by v2
frozen_control.writer_and_annotator: The same GenericModelOutput Writer and render product contract used by v2

single_changed_factor: Replace the v2 synchronous standalone SimulationApp update loop with the NVIDIA-tested Kit async test lifecycle: AsyncTestCase-compatible setup, create_new_stage_async, wait_for_viewport_async, timeline play, exactly 300 next_update_async calls, timeline stop, and one final next_update_async flush.
implementation_plan_after_approval: Implement a minimal project-owned Kit async control test and runner that preserve the v2 asset, scene, pose, Writer, image, network and metrics. Freeze code hashes, add contract/unit tests, submit a smoke card and run spec, run all V3 tests and preflight, then report those results before the one permitted GPU execution.

decision_rule.pass: More than zero Writer callbacks, valid GMO headers and positive-element payloads prove that the pinned async Kit runtime is healthy; the failure is then isolated to synchronous standalone scheduling, and project capture must adopt or wrap the async execution model only after a separate design review.
decision_rule.callback_zero: Successful async setup, viewport readiness, sensor creation, Writer attach and exactly 300 async updates with zero callback provide stronger evidence that the pinned host/headless Replicator runtime is blocked beyond the standalone loop.
decision_rule.setup_failure: Failure before viewport readiness, sensor creation or Writer attach is classified as async-control implementation/startup failure and does not diagnose LiDAR output health. Stop without retry.

stop_rule: One execution only after a separate explicit user approval and frozen preflight. No retry, network, asset change, scene change, sensor substitution, saved point sample, Cano, formal data, label, training, model, topology or M-TARE work. Any setup, hash, callback, GMO, evidence or timeout failure stops the task and is reported.

estimated_cost.compute: After approval only: one short headless RTX GPU Kit async test in the pinned network-disabled Isaac Sim 6.0.1 image. Current proposal creation uses no GPU.

retirement.confirmation_reference: After the Isaac failure boundary and CPU-raycast replacement were explained, the user approved continuing without Isaac: 那就继续吧
retirement.reason: Isaac is not a research contribution and is no longer allowed to block the procedural-topology supervision route. The unresolved async control remains valid optional failure evidence but will not be implemented or executed on the current critical path.
